newsitem.title: USA: Senate panel backs Barshefsky as U.S. Trade Rep.
newsitem.headline: Senate panel backs Barshefsky as U.S. Trade Rep.

text.p: The U.S. Senate Finance Committee on Thursday voted to recommend Charlene Barshefsky for the position of U.S. Trade Representative.

The panel also voted in favor of a waiver of a 1995 law that prevents those who have worked for foreign governments from holding the post. As a private attorney, Barshefsky advised Canada in 1990 on a lumber dispute with the United States.
The full Senate must vote on the nomination for Barshefsky to be confirmed. Both the House of Representatives and the Senate must approve the waiver.
President Bill Clinton nominated Barshefsky to the position.
She has been the United States' top trade negotiator in an acting capacity since last April, when she succeeded Mickey Kantor.
